## RANGE_SESSIONIZE
# Source: BigQuery range-functions#range_sessionize specifies connected sessions,
# retaining input rows, with MEETS including touching bounds and OVERLAPS excluding them.
# RANGE's unbounded ends follow data-types#range_type. These cases apply those rules.

# A contained range must not hide an earlier, longer range from the running end.
WITH ranges AS (SELECT 1 AS id, RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-01, 2024-01-10)' AS r UNION ALL SELECT 2, RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-02, 2024-01-03)' UNION ALL SELECT 3, RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-09, 2024-01-12)') SELECT STRING_AGG(CAST(session_range AS STRING), ';' ORDER BY id) FROM RANGE_SESSIONIZE(TABLE ranges, 'r', [], 'OVERLAPS')
=> "[2024-01-01, 2024-01-12);[2024-01-01, 2024-01-12);[2024-01-01, 2024-01-12)"

# Transitive overlap; duplicate rows are retained, even when only the added column is read.
WITH ranges AS (SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-01, 2024-01-03)' AS r UNION ALL SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-02, 2024-01-04)' UNION ALL SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-03, 2024-01-05)' UNION ALL SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-03, 2024-01-05)') SELECT STRING_AGG(CAST(session_range AS STRING), ';') FROM RANGE_SESSIONIZE(TABLE ranges, 'r', [], 'OVERLAPS')
=> "[2024-01-01, 2024-01-05);[2024-01-01, 2024-01-05);[2024-01-01, 2024-01-05);[2024-01-01, 2024-01-05)"

# Unbounded ranges meet at their finite boundary in MEETS.
WITH ranges AS (SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[UNBOUNDED, 2024-01-03)' AS r UNION ALL SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-03, UNBOUNDED)') SELECT STRING_AGG(CAST(session_range AS STRING), ';') FROM RANGE_SESSIONIZE(TABLE ranges, 'r', [])
=> "[UNBOUNDED, UNBOUNDED);[UNBOUNDED, UNBOUNDED)"

WITH ranges AS (SELECT 1 AS id, RANGE<DATE> '[UNBOUNDED, 2024-01-03)' AS r UNION ALL SELECT 2, RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-03, UNBOUNDED)') SELECT STRING_AGG(CAST(session_range AS STRING), ';' ORDER BY id) FROM RANGE_SESSIONIZE(TABLE ranges, 'r', [], 'OVERLAPS')
=> "[UNBOUNDED, 2024-01-03);[2024-01-03, UNBOUNDED)"

# Separate partitions do not merge touching ranges.
WITH ranges AS (SELECT 1 AS id, 'a' AS p, 1 AS k, RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-01, 2024-01-03)' AS r UNION ALL SELECT 2, 'a', 2, RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-03, 2024-01-05)' UNION ALL SELECT 3, 'b', 1, RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-03, 2024-01-05)') SELECT STRING_AGG(CAST(session_range AS STRING), ';' ORDER BY id) FROM RANGE_SESSIONIZE(TABLE ranges, 'r', ['p', 'k'])
=> "[2024-01-01, 2024-01-03);[2024-01-03, 2024-01-05);[2024-01-03, 2024-01-05)"

# DATETIME bounds retain microseconds, and a disjoint range starts another session.
WITH ranges AS (SELECT 1 AS id, RANGE<DATETIME> '[2024-01-01 00:00:00.000001, 2024-01-01 00:00:00.000002)' AS r UNION ALL SELECT 2, RANGE<DATETIME> '[2024-01-01 00:00:00.000002, 2024-01-01 00:00:00.000003)' UNION ALL SELECT 3, RANGE<DATETIME> '[2024-01-01 00:00:00.000004, UNBOUNDED)') SELECT STRING_AGG(CAST(session_range AS STRING), ';' ORDER BY id) FROM RANGE_SESSIONIZE(TABLE ranges, 'r', [], 'MEETS')
=> "[2024-01-01 00:00:00.000001, 2024-01-01 00:00:00.000003);[2024-01-01 00:00:00.000001, 2024-01-01 00:00:00.000003);[2024-01-01 00:00:00.000004, UNBOUNDED)"

# TIMESTAMP sessionization uses instants, including pre-epoch fractional bounds.
WITH ranges AS (SELECT RANGE<TIMESTAMP> '[1969-12-31 23:59:59.999999+00, 1970-01-01 00:00:00+00)' AS r UNION ALL SELECT RANGE<TIMESTAMP> '[1970-01-01 00:00:00+00, 1970-01-01 00:00:00.000001+00)') SELECT STRING_AGG(CAST(session_range AS STRING), ';') FROM RANGE_SESSIONIZE(TABLE ranges, 'r', [])
=> "[1969-12-31 23:59:59.999999+00, 1970-01-01 00:00:00.000001+00);[1969-12-31 23:59:59.999999+00, 1970-01-01 00:00:00.000001+00)"

WITH ranges AS (SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-01, 2024-01-03)' AS r LIMIT 0) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM RANGE_SESSIONIZE(TABLE ranges, 'r', [])
=> "0"

# Confirmed against BigQuery by the maintainer.

WITH ranges AS (SELECT 1 AS id, CAST(NULL AS RANGE<DATE>) AS r UNION ALL SELECT 2, RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-01, 2024-02-01)') SELECT ARRAY_AGG(STRUCT(id, CAST(session_range AS STRING) AS session_range) ORDER BY id) FROM RANGE_SESSIONIZE(TABLE ranges, 'r', [])
=> [{"v":{"f":[{"v":"1"},{"v":null}]}},{"v":{"f":[{"v":"2"},{"v":"[2024-01-01, 2024-02-01)"}]}}]

WITH ranges AS (SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-01, 2024-02-01)' AS r) SELECT session_range FROM RANGE_SESSIONIZE(TABLE ranges, 'r', [], 'meets')
=> error contains: Could not cast literal "meets" to type RANGE_SESSIONIZE_MODE; Did you mean 'MEETS'? (Note: ENUM values are case sensitive)

WITH ranges AS (SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-01, 2024-02-01)' AS r, 1 AS session_range) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM RANGE_SESSIONIZE(TABLE ranges, 'r', [])
=> "1"

WITH ranges AS (SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-01, 2024-02-01)' AS r, 1 AS session_range) SELECT (SELECT AS STRUCT * FROM RANGE_SESSIONIZE(TABLE ranges, 'r', []))
=> {"f":[{"v":"[2024-01-01, 2024-02-01)"},{"v":"[2024-01-01, 2024-02-01)"}]}

# The range column names a RANGE column of the input, and each partitioning column one of its
# columns.
# third_party/bigquery_docs/reference/standard-sql/range-functions.md
WITH ranges AS (SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-01, 2024-02-01)' AS r) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM RANGE_SESSIONIZE(TABLE ranges, 'missing', [])
=> error:

WITH ranges AS (SELECT 1 AS k, RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-01, 2024-02-01)' AS r) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM RANGE_SESSIONIZE(TABLE ranges, 'k', [])
=> error:

WITH ranges AS (SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-01, 2024-02-01)' AS r) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM RANGE_SESSIONIZE(TABLE ranges, 'r', ['missing'])
=> error:

WITH ranges AS (SELECT RANGE<DATE> '[2024-01-01, 2024-02-01)' AS r) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM RANGE_SESSIONIZE(TABLE ranges, 'r', [], 'invalid')
=> error:
